correctness.rationale: For arbitrary n>=2 and 2<=k<=n, conditional pi(i)=i image-sampling gives per-subset probability K_{i,r}/(n-1)_{k-1}; counting K_{i,r} subsets yields B/(k-1)! times sum of squared hypergeometric ranks. Subtract B/k!, multiply by 1/n and use Vandermonde to get the sum-of-squares formula. Endpoint and strict binomial log-concavity give all strict signs; beta integrals and a central-binomial convolution yield the fixed-k limit. Exact arithmetic replay from the embedded verify.py passed 2814 comparisons including all 46232 permutations n=2..8. Finite checks supplement, not prove, the all-n theorem.

originality.rationale: The measured object is the cross-moment of fixed-point indicators and the count of nonconsecutive increasing length-k subsequences. Pinsky arxiv:math/0407353 defines Z and mu but reports Z mean/variance and TV, not this local squared-rank identity. Hossein–Starr extends the Z second moment, and Diaconis–Evans–Graham concerns consecutive unseparated pairs. The closest accessible comparison claims concern consecutive rank patterns, descents, or inversions. The 1981 Lifschitz–Pittel full text remained unavailable, so earlier priority remains a named limitation.

value.rationale: Pinsky introduced a natural size bias by nonconsecutive monotone subsequence counts; the theorem measures the previously unquantified fixed-point mean response, proves nonnegativity at every position and exact exceptional equality, and represents the signal as hypergeometric rank dispersion. The asymptotic covariance scale and constant at every fixed k and the complete range through k=n are structural information not implied by the marginal formula or a routine change of parameters. Full stochastic domination and k-growing asymptotics are not claimed.
